extracted.intended_audience: general readers, TV viewers, critics, and researchers interested in the series Barry
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style article summarizing the television series Barry: episode summaries, production history, viewership/rating data, critical reception, and awards/nominations. Useful for readers seeking facts about the show's performance and recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotten Tomatoes score and critical consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Season- and series-level percentage of positive critic reviews and average rating reported by Rotten Tomatoes; includes a short critical consensus statement summarizing critics' view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the page: 'On Rotten Tomatoes, the first season holds a 98% rating with an average rating of 8.1/10...Critical consensus: "PTSD and comedy make strangely endearing bedfellows in Barry, which proves more poignant than its sketch show premise."' Other season consensus lines include: 'Barry follows up a pitch-perfect debut with a second season that balances darkness with comedy while steering clear of antihero overindulgence.'; 'Bill Hader and company can take a well-deserved bow—Barry makes its belated return to the screen without missing a step, retaining its edge as one of television’s funniest and most unsettling offerings.'; 'What began as a macabre comedy is now close to completely shorn of genuine mirth, but Bill Hader's masterful indictment of stardom closes the curtain with one hell of an encore.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Metacritic score (weighted average)
rubrics_metrics.description: Season-level weighted average score out of 100 compiled by Metacritic, with an interpretation (e.g., 'universal acclaim').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the page: Season 1 — 84 (30 reviews) indicating 'universal acclaim'; Season 2 — 87 (14 reviews); Season 3 — 94 (19 reviews); Season 4 — 90 (23 reviews). Used as a critical-evaluation metric alongside Rotten Tomatoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nielsen viewership and ratings metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Per-episode Nielsen ratings and viewership numbers reported on the page (rating in 18–49 demo, viewers in millions, DVR numbers where available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists per-episode data such as 'Rating (18–49)', 'Viewers (millions)', 'DVR (18–49)', 'DVR viewers (millions)', 'Total (18–49)', and 'Total viewers (millions)'. Example: S2 Episode 6: '0.8 / 1.99 million' and for other episodes precise figures are tabulated. These metrics are presented as measures of audience size and commercial performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement on critics' 'best TV' lists and legacy rankings
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion and ranking on publications' lists of greatest TV shows (an indicator of critical legacy and prestige).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes placements such as 'no. 91 by Empire, no. 53 by IGN, and no. 52 by Rolling Stone' in various lists of the 100 greatest TV shows of all time. Such placements function as evaluative recognition beyond season-by-season reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Comedy Series (overall series-level award)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition for the series as a whole in awards that honor the best comedy series (e.g., Primetime Emmy Award — Outstanding Comedy Series; Golden Globe Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists nominations and wins for 'Outstanding Comedy Series' and similar top-level awards, and cites producers/creatives named on nominations (e.g., Alec Berg, Bill Hader, producers). Used to evaluate the series' overall excellence in the comedy category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series (acting — lead)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award category assessing excellence of a lead actor's performance in a comedy series (e.g., Bill Hader nominated/won for specific episodes/seasons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Bill Hader 'Won' (for 'Chapter Seven: Loud, Fast And Keep Going') and other nominations listed. The article records which performances/episodes were cited for nominations/wins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Supporting Actor/Actress in a Comedy Series (acting — supporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award categories assessing excellence of supporting performances in the series (e.g., Henry Winkler, Anthony Carrigan, Sarah Goldberg listed as nominees/winners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page: Henry Winkler 'Won' (for 'Chapter Four: Commit To You'); Anthony Carrigan and others nominated; specific episodes cited when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directing for a Comedy Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Award category assessing excellence in directing individual episodes of the comedy series (Primetime Emmy/Directors Guild citations appear on the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Bill Hader nominated/won for directing ('Chapter One: Make Your Mark'; 'ronny/lily'); Alec Berg also nominated. Episodes associated with directing nominations/wins are listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for a Comedy Series (episodic writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award category recognizing excellence in writing for the series, often tied to specific episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists nominations/wins for writing for episodes such as 'Chapter One: Make Your Mark', 'ronny/lily', 'starting now', and others; both individual writers and writer teams are named. Used to evaluate narrative and script quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-camera picture editing (comedy series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recognition for excellence in picture editing on single-camera half-hour comedy episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Jeff Buchanan nominated for 'Chapter One: Make Your Mark'; Ali Greer won for 'starting now'; Kyle Reiter nominated for 'berkman > block'. The page records nominations/wins tied to specific episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound editing and sound mixing (television series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award categories assessing the technical quality of sound editing and mixing on episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists nominees and winners for 'Outstanding Sound Editing' and 'Outstanding Sound Mixing' for episodes such as 'Chapter Seven: Loud, Fast And Keep Going' and 'ronny/lily'. These are presented as technical criteria in awards evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cinematography for a single-camera series (half-hour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award category recognizing excellence in cinematography for half-hour single-camera television episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Paula Huidobro nominated/won for 'Chapter Eight: Know Your Truth' (Primetime Creative Arts Emmy nomination). The page records cinematography nominations per episode/season.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production design for a narrative program (half-hour or less)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recognition for production design excellence in short-form narrative television episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page entries include nominations for Tyler B. Robinson, Eric Schoonover, and others for episodes like 'Chapter Seven: Loud, Fast And Keep Going' and 'ronny/lily'. Used to evaluate sets, art direction, and visual world-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting (television series casting excellence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award category evaluating the quality of casting choices for the series (e.g., Outstanding Casting for a Comedy Series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists casting directors Sharon Bialy and Sherry Thomas (and others) as nominees for Outstanding Casting. Casting awards indicate how well roles were filled and ensemble effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music composition for a series (original dramatic score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recognition for original music composition in television episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists David Wingo nominated for 'What?' (Outstanding Music Composition for a Series). Used to evaluate the series' original music and scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stunt coordination and stunt achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Award category evaluating stunt coordination and stunt work in the series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes nominations for 'Outstanding Stunt Coordination for a Comedy Series or Variety Program' (e.g., Wade Allen nominated). This measures the quality and safety/execution of action sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival screenings and premiere/events as recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection/screening at festivals and premiere events used as markers of industry interest and early critical exposure (e.g., Series Mania screening).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes that episodes one through three were screened during the Series Mania Festival and that the series held an official premiere at NeueHouse Hollywood. Festival/programming inclusion functions as early validation and publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical qualitative criteria highlighted in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative/tonal qualities critics repeatedly emphasized as strengths or weaknesses (balance of darkness and comedy, handling of PTSD themes, avoidance of antihero overindulgence, maintaining edge, thematic indictment of stardom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted critic phrases on the page serve as guidance for what constituted 'success' in critics' eyes: e.g., 'PTSD and comedy make strangely endearing bedfellows', 'balances darkness with comedy while steering clear of antihero overindulgence', 'retaining its edge as one of television’s funniest and most unsettling offerings', 'masterful indictment of stardom'. These phrases indicate the qualitative standards critics used when evaluating the show's tone, theme integration, and moral framing.
